t:
(a) In General.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, including the Surplus Property Act of 1944 (58 Stat. 765, chapter 479; 50 U.S.C. App. 1622 et seq.), and subject to the requirements of this section, the Secretary (or the appropriate Federal officer) may waive, without charge, any of the terms contained in any deed of conveyance described in subsection (b) that restrict the use of any land described in such a deed that, as of the date of the enactment of this Act, is not being used for the operation of an airport or for air traffic. A waiver made under the preceding sentence shall be deemed to be consistent with the requirements of section 47153 of title 49, United States Code. 
    (b) Deed of Conveyance.—A deed of conveyance referred to in subsection (a) is a deed of conveyance issued by the United States before the date of the enactment of this Act for the conveyance of lands to a public institution of higher education in Oklahoma. 
    (c) Use of Lands Subject to Waiver.—

        (1) In general.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the lands subject to a waiver under subsection (a) shall not be subject to any term, condition, reservation, or restriction that would otherwise apply to that land as a result of the conveyance of that land by the United States to the institution of higher education. 
        (2) Use of revenues.—An institution of higher education that is issued a waiver under subsection (a) shall use revenues derived from the use, operation, or disposal of that land—

            (A) for the airport; and 
            (B) to the extent that funds remain available, for weather-related and educational purposes that primarily benefit aviation.   
    (d) Condition.—An institution of higher education that is issued a waiver under subsection (a), shall agree that, in leasing or conveying any interest in land to which the deed of conveyance described in subsection (b) relates, the institution will receive an amount that is equal to the fair lease value or the fair market value, as the case may be, as determined pursuant to regulations issued by the Secretary. 
    (e) Grants.—

        (1) In general.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, if an institution of higher education that is subject to a waiver under subsection (a) received financial assistance in the form of a grant from the Federal Aviation Administration or a predecessor agency before the date of the enactment of this Act, then the Secretary may waive the repayment of the outstanding amount of any grant that the institution of higher education would otherwise be required to pay. 
        (2) Eligibility to receive subsequent grants.—Nothing in paragraph (1) shall affect the eligibility of an institution of higher education that is subject to that paragraph from receiving grants from the Secretary under chapter 471 of title 49, United States Code, or under any other provision of law relating to financial assistance provided through the Federal Aviation Administration.

fable.w: The waiver itself and the institution's agreement to conditions are not participation; they resemble a benefit granted to a recipient, and no outside party is consulted on the waiver decision. However, subsection (d) provides that fair lease or market value is determined under regulations issued by the Secretary, and a statute's contemplation of agency rulemaking is treated as participation because rulemaking brings in public comment. This is a close call, since the phrase may simply refer to existing regulations rather than authorising or requiring new ones.
fable.s: as determined pursuant to regulations issued by the Secretary

qwen_block.w: This section grants the Secretary of Transportation the authority to waive deed restrictions for specific institutions of higher education. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public comment, or the involvement of non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The interaction is strictly between the federal agency and the recipient of the waiver (the institution), which constitutes an administrative action or benefit rather than participation in a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary (or the appropriate Federal officer) may waive, without charge, any of the terms contained in any deed of conveyance described in subsection (b) that restrict the use of any land described in such a deed

opus.w: Subsection (d) has the Secretary set fair lease and fair market value through regulations. The definition counts required or authorized rulemaking as participation because it brings in public comment (see Example 6). It is tempting to say 'No' because the rest of the section only covers waivers and grant repayment for one university, which are benefit decisions, not participation. But the rulemaking reference is enough on its own to make this a 'Yes'.
opus.s: the institution will receive an amount that is equal to the fair lease value or the fair market value, as the case may be, as determined pursuant to regulations issued by the Secretary
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** answer "No." Most of this section covers a waiver of deed restrictions given to an Oklahoma public university, and the waiver of repayment for old grants. Those are benefits granted to a single outside party, and benefit or grant decisions don't count as participation.

2. **Why that fails:** subsection (d) says fair lease value or fair market value will be "determined pursuant to regulations issued by the Secretary." The definition counts "requiring rulemaking" as participation, and Example 6 treats a grant of power to make regulations the same way. Rulemaking brings a public comment process with it. The reference here is brief and implies the regulations rather than ordering them outright, so I'm only moderately confident.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary the authority to waive deed restrictions for specific institutions. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory committees before making this decision. The interaction described is administrative (waiving conditions on a grant/deed), which falls under the exclusion for applications for benefits or grants.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary (or the appropriate Federal officer) may waive, without charge, any of the terms contained in any deed of conveyance described in subsection (b) that restrict the use of any land described in such a deed
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the institution to "agree" to certain terms in subsection (d) constitutes participation. However, this is a condition of receiving a waiver (a benefit), not a process for the institution to influence a federal policy decision or consult with the government before a decision is made. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants. The core action here is the Secretary's unilateral authority to waive deed restrictions.
